info.description:
Complete API collection for Marketplace Ethiopia with sample data

**Base URLs:**
- Local: http://127.0.0.1:8030
- Production: https://www.marketplace.et

**Authentication:**
Most endpoints require Bearer token. Login first to get your token.

**All requests include sample data - ready to test!**

🌐 **Public Endpoint**\n\nEndpoint: `POST /api/login`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\AccountController@login`

**Security note:** an unregistered email and a wrong password for a real account both return the exact same `401` response (`"Invalid email or password."`) — this is intentional, so the endpoint can't be used to discover which emails have accounts (account enumeration).

🌐 **Public Endpoint**\n\nEndpoint: `GET /api/verify/{email}/{token}`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\AccountController@verifyAccount`

**Idempotent:** if the account is already verified (e.g. the user clicked an older email after a newer one already verified them, or double-clicked the same link), this returns the same `200` success response instead of a `400` token-mismatch error.

request.description:
🌐 **Public Endpoint**\n\nEndpoint: `POST /api/resend-verification`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\AccountController@resendVerification`

**Reuses the existing token** if one is already pending, instead of generating a new one — so a previous verification email the user still has open stays valid. A new token is only generated if none exists yet.

400 – Invalid or already verified account

request.description:
🌐 **Public Endpoint**

Endpoint: `POST /api/auth/apple`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\AccountController@appleLogin`

**Sign in with Apple — mobile SDK flow.**

The client app obtains an `identity_token` (JWT) from Apple's SDK and sends it here. Apple only provides `email` and `full_name` on the **very first sign-in** — pass them through on that call or they are lost permanently.

**Fields:**
- `identity_token` *(required)* — JWT from Apple's `ASAuthorizationAppleIDCredential.identityToken`
- `full_name` *(first sign-in only)* — from `ASAuthorizationAppleIDCredential.fullName`
- `email` *(first sign-in only)* — may be a relay address (`@privaterelay.appleid.com`)
- `device_name` *(optional)* — used to label the Sanctum token

request.description:
🌐 **Public Endpoint**

Endpoint: `GET /api/adverts/{id}`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\AdvertController@show`

Returns full advert details (images, category/sub-category/brand, car/phone-specific details, owner info, related adverts).

**URL Parameter:**
- `id` — The advert's database `id` (integer, primary key — NOT the public-facing `ad_id` shown in share links)

**Errors — the endpoint never redirects; it always returns JSON:**
- `404` `{"reason": "not_found"}` — no advert exists with that `id`
- `410` `{"reason": "blocked"}` — advert was flagged and permanently blocked
- `410` `{"reason": "removed_by_admin"}` — advert was hidden by an admin (not deleted)

Same visibility rules as the web ad page (`App\Support\AdvertVisibility`), but the web page redirects to the homepage on any of these — this endpoint returns a structured error instead so the app can show an in-place "ad no longer available" state.

response.name: 404 — Advert not found
410 — Advert no longer available

- `per_page` (optional, default 20, max 40)

🌐 **Public Endpoint**

Endpoint: `GET /api/categories/{category_slug}`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\AdvertController@categoryAdverts`

Returns paginated ads for a category using `FeaturedAdPaginator`. Page 1 includes featured/boosted ads. Also returns the list of subcategories with ad counts and icons.

**Response shape:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "ads": [...],
    "cat": {...},
    "count_cat": 120,
    "subcategories": [
      {
        "id": 2,
        "sub_category": "Cars",
        "sub_cat_slug": "cars",
        "icon": "cars.png",
        "icon_url": "https://.../frontend/images/subcategory-icons/cars.png",
        "advert_count": 12500
      }
    ]
  },
  "pagination": {
    "has_more": true,
    "next_page": 2,
    "current_page": 1,
    "per_page": 24,
    "total": 120,
    "last_page": 5
  }
}
```

**Notes:**
- `subcategories[].icon_url` is `null` when no admin icon has been uploaded
- Subcategories are sorted by `advert_count` descending

📱 **Mobile Endpoint — Public**

Endpoint: `GET /api/categories/{category_slug}/subcategories`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\AdvertController@categorySubcategories`

Returns all subcategories under a category with live ad counts, an admin-uploaded icon, and a representative thumbnail image from the first active ad in each subcategory. Designed for the mobile category-browse screen (subcategory list view).

**Path params:**
- `category_slug` — e.g. `vehicles`, `phones-tablets`

**Response shape:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "category": {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Vehicles",
    "slug": "vehicles",
    "total_ads": 45230
  },
  "subcategories": [
    {
      "id": 2,
      "name": "Cars",
      "slug": "cars",
      "advert_count": 12500,
      "icon_url": "https://.../frontend/images/subcategory-icons/cars.png",
      "thumbnail_url": "https://..."
    }
  ],
  "total": 8
}
```

**Icon priority (recommended display order):**
1. `icon_url` — admin-uploaded icon (PNG/WebP, shown at 60×60 px on mobile)
2. `thumbnail_url` — first active ad image for that subcategory
3. Fallback SVG placeholder in your app if both are `null`

**Notes:**
- Subcategories are sorted **alphabetically** by name
- `icon_url` is `null` when no admin icon has been uploaded for that subcategory
- `thumbnail_url` is `null` if no active ads exist in that subcategory
- `advert_count` only counts active, non-recently-sold ads
- No pagination — all subcategories returned in a single response

🌐 **Public Endpoint**

Endpoint: `POST /api/search`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\SearchController@search`

**Request Body:**
- `product` (string, optional, min 3 chars): Search term
- `location` (string, optional): State name (e.g. `Addis Ababa`)
- `category` (integer, optional): Category ID
- `sub_category` (integer, optional): Sub-category ID
- `brand` (integer, optional): Brand ID
- `buydirect` (string, optional): `yes` or `no`
- `item_condition` (string, optional): See condition values below
- `per_page` (integer, optional, default 20)
- `page` (integer, optional, default 1)

**`item_condition` values:**
- General categories: `New`, `Foreign Used`, `Locally Used`
- Vehicles (category 1): `Local used`, `Foreign used`
- Phones & Tablets (category 4): `New - Unboxed`, `New - No Packaging`, `Used - Very Good`, `Used - Good`, `Used - Defect`, `Foreign Used - No Packaging`

> The correct table is chosen automatically based on `category`.

🌐 **Public Endpoint — Unified Filter (replaces all filter-by-* endpoints)**

Endpoint: `POST /api/search/filter`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\SearchController@filter`

All parameters are optional. Pass only the ones you need. Car/phone detail joins only activate when their specific params are present.

**General Parameters:**
- `keyword` (string, optional) — search term, matches ad title or ad_id
- `category` (integer, optional) — Category ID
- `sub_category` (integer, optional) — Sub-category ID
- `brand` (integer, optional) — Brand ID
- `location` (string, optional) — State name e.g. `Addis Ababa`
- `per_page` (integer, optional, default 20)
- `page` (integer, optional, default 1)

**Price Parameters** (use `min`/`max` OR `range`, not both):
- `min` (integer, optional) — minimum price
- `max` (integer, optional) — maximum price
- `range` (string, optional) — `under_20k` \| `20k_120k` \| `120k_1m` \| `1m_10m` \| `above_10m`

**Listing Type Parameters:**
- `buydirect` (string, optional) — `Yes` or `No`
- `seller` (string, optional) — `all` \| `verified` \| `unverified`
- `item_condition` (string, optional) — general condition for non-car, non-phone categories: `New` \| `Foreign Used` \| `Locally Used`

**Vehicle-Specific Parameters** (category 1 — Vehicles):
- `car_condition` (string or array, optional) — `Local used` \| `Foreign used`
- `fuel_type` (string or array, optional) — `Petrol` \| `Diesel` \| `Electric` \| `Hybrid` \| `Natural gas CNG` \| `LPG`
- `transmission` (string or array, optional) — `Automatic` \| `Manual` \| `AMT` \| `CVT`
- `registration` (string or array, optional) — `Registered` \| `Unregistered`

**Phone-Specific Parameters** (category 4 — Mobile Phones & Tablets):
- `phone_condition` (string or array, optional) — `New - Unboxed` \| `New - No Packaging` \| `Used - Very Good` \| `Used - Good` \| `Used - Defect` \| `Foreign Used - No Packaging`
- `device_type` (string or array, optional) — `Smartphone` \| `Feature Phone` \| `Tablet`

**Response includes `filters_applied`** — echoes back only the filters that were active in the query.

> The old endpoints (`filter-by-seller`, `filter-by-buydirect`, `filter-by-car`, `filter-by-phone`) still work for backward compatibility but this single endpoint should be used for all new development.

Endpoint: `DELETE /api/adverts/{advertId}`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\UserManageAdverts@deleteAdvert`

Delete an advert and all associated images

🌐 **Public Endpoint** (no auth required)

Endpoint: `GET /api/adverts/image-requirements`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\UserManageAdverts@imageRequirements`

Returns the admin-configured image requirements (count, dimensions, file size, format) that the server enforces when creating/updating an advert. Cached ~1hr server-side per setting; safe for the client to cache too.

The same object is also embedded under `data.image_requirements` in `GET /api/adverts/create/data`.

**Field reference:**
- `min_images` / `max_images` — number of images required/allowed per advert (not applied to Jobs/CV categories)
- `min_width` / `min_height` — images below this resolution are rejected
- `recommended_width` / `recommended_height` — images below this (but above the minimum) are accepted with a quality warning
- `min_file_size_bytes` / `max_file_size_bytes` — file size bounds in bytes
- `max_file_size_kb` — same max, in kilobytes
- `allowed_formats` — accepted image mime subtypes
- `strictness` — 1–10, how strictly the server's own quality checks (blur, brightness, overall score) are applied; informational, not something the client needs to replicate

**Mobile Implementation:**
1. Fetch on "Post Ad" screen load (or reuse the value already returned by `create/data`)
2. Validate images client-side against these numbers before upload — count, resolution, file size — and show one clear message per rule
3. Don't hardcode these numbers; they change whenever the admin updates settings
4. The server still re-validates on upload/create — this endpoint lets the client match those rules, it doesn't replace server-side enforcement

Endpoint: `POST /api/user/payments/{paymentId}/resume`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\UserController@resumePayment`

Mobile equivalent of the web **Complete Payment** button on My Orders. Re-initializes a Flutterwave transaction for an abandoned (pending) payment and returns a fresh `authorization_url`.

**URL Parameter:**
- `paymentId` — The payment record `id` (integer). Get this from the pending orders list.

**No request body required.**

**Mobile flow:**
1. Show pending orders (payments with `payment_status = pending`)
2. User taps **Complete Payment** → call this endpoint
3. On success, open `authorization_url` in an in-app browser / WebView
4. Flutterwave calls the callback URL after payment — order is marked paid automatically
5. Redirect user back to My Orders screen

**Authorization:**
- Returns `404` if the payment does not belong to the authenticated user or is not pending
- Returns `409` if the ad has already been sold to another buyer
- Returns `502` if Flutterwave fails to initialize

4. Apply subcategory rules ON TOP of category rules

6. Mark fields in `required` array as mandatory

item.name: 10. Advertising
item.description:
**Public Advertising Endpoints**

Fetch and display active advertisement banners and sidebars in the mobile app.

**No authentication required.**

**Ad Types:**

**Integration Notes:**
- Poll this endpoint at app launch and cache for session duration
- Open `url` in an in-app browser on tap
- Record clicks via the click endpoint for analytics
